added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(T\in\mathbb N\), \(0<\rho\le T\), and \(w>0\), the corrected occupation-measure Lagrange value obeys
\[
\mathcal D_{T,\rho}(w)\le\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w).
\]
This weak-duality inequality requires neither strong duality nor attainment.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a baseline \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\), a primal-feasible occupation family \(\nu=(\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a})\), and dual-feasible \((\lambda,\zeta_P,\xi_P)\).  Write
\[
N_P=\sum_{\mathsf Q:(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(\mathsf Q)
\]
and let \(C_P\) denote the welfare integral in the third constraint of \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\).  The information constraint defining \(\mathcal R_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)\), integrated against the finite nonnegative measure \(\lambda_{P,\mathsf Q}\), gives
\[
\kappa_\delta\lambda_{P,\mathsf Q}(\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w))
\le
\int_{\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int_{\mathsf Q}k_a(P,P';x)
\,d\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x)\,d\lambda_{P,\mathsf Q}(P').
\]
Because \(\lambda_{P,\mathsf Q}\) has finite support and every integrand is nonnegative, interchange of the finite sum and the nonnegative integrals is valid.  Summing over active cells and applying the pointwise dual constraint yields
\[
\begin{split}
\kappa_\delta\sum_{\mathsf Q}
\lambda_{P,\mathsf Q}(\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w))
&\le N_P
+\sum_{\mathsf Q,a}\int_{\mathsf Q}\zeta_P(x)
\,d\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x)+\xi_PC_P.
\end{split}
\]
The context-arrival domination in the primal and nonnegativity of \(\zeta_P\) imply, first for nonnegative simple functions and then by monotone convergence,
\[
\sum_{\mathsf Q,a}\int_{\mathsf Q}\zeta_P(x)
\,d\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x)
\le T\int_{\mathcal X}\zeta_P(x)\,dP_X(x).
\]
The welfare constraint gives \(C_P\le\rho\), and \(\xi_P\ge0\).  Rearrangement therefore gives
\[
\kappa_\delta\sum_{\mathsf Q}
\lambda_{P,\mathsf Q}(\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w))
-T\int\zeta_P\,dP_X-\rho\xi_P\le N_P.
\]
Taking the supremum over dual-feasible variables, then the infimum over primal-feasible occupations, proves the baselinewise inequality; it remains valid when the primal feasible set is empty because its value is \(+\infty\).  Taking the supremum over \(P\) on both sides gives \(\mathcal D_{T,\rho}(w)\le\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\), as claimed.
added_lemmas.justification: Weak duality certifies that the displayed price program is a valid lower relaxation without assuming the unresolved strong-duality step.
added_lemmas.gap: The prior scalar-count dual did not include context-arrival or welfare constraints; this result handles both through their Lagrange prices.
added_lemmas.consumer: The saturation question can use dual feasible points as certified lower bounds on the corrected occupation demand.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(w>0\), if \(\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) and \(I_T\in\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) satisfy
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}}
\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|\le w,
\]
then the design-induced baseline-indexed occupation measures are feasible in \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\), and hence \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\le T\).  Consequently,
\[
\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\ge\frac{2w_{T,\rho}}{1-2\delta}
\quad\text{and}\quad
W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\ge w_{T,\rho},
\]
with the extended-real conventions in the definitions.  These are necessary relaxation bounds only; they assert no sequential realization of a baseline-specific feasible profile.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a baseline \(P\), a cell \(\mathsf Q\), an arm \(a\), and a non-anticipating design \(\mathsf D\).  For every Borel \(E\subseteq\mathcal X\), define the design-induced finite occupation measure
\[
\nu^{\mathsf D}_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(E)
=\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}\sum_{t=1}^T
\mathbf 1\{X_t\in E\cap\mathsf Q,A_t=a\}.
\]
It is nonnegative, finite, and supported on \(\mathsf Q\).  Because exactly one arm is selected each round and the contexts have common marginal \(P_X\), for every Borel \(E\),
\[
\sum_{\mathsf Q:(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\nu^{\mathsf D}_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(E)
\le\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf 1\{X_t\in E\}
=T P_X(E).
\]
By the welfare-loss identity and nonnegativity of its summands,
\[
\sum_{\mathsf Q:(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int_{\mathsf Q}
|\tau_P(x)|\mathbf 1\{a\ne\pi_P^\star(x)\}
\,d\nu^{\mathsf D}_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x)
\le\mathcal R_T(P,\mathsf D)\le\rho,
\]
where the last inequality is the uniform budget condition defining \(\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\).

Now take \(P'\in\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)\).  The laws have the same context marginal and their arm means agree off \(\mathsf Q\).  Therefore the exact adaptive Gaussian likelihood decomposition in the already-established coverage--information converse and the definition of the occupation measure give
\[
\mathrm{KL}(\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}\Vert\mathbb P_{P',\mathsf D}^{T})
=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int_{\mathsf Q}
k_a(P,P';x)\,d\nu^{\mathsf D}_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x).
\]
Suppose the interval in the statement has worst-law expected length at most \(w\).  If the last display were at most \(\kappa_\delta\), the coverage--information converse would imply
\[
\max\left\{\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T|,
\mathbb E_{P',\mathsf D}|I_T|\right\}
\ge\frac{1-2\delta}{2}|\theta(P)-\theta(P')|>w,
\]
contradicting the assumed worst-law bound.  Hence the displayed information is strictly larger than \(\kappa_\delta\) for every local alternative.  The induced occupations belong to every required \(\mathcal R_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)\), obey the capacity and welfare constraints above, and have total mass at most \(T\).  Taking the inner infimum and then the supremum over baselines proves \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\le T\).

It remains to derive the two numerical lower bounds.  If \(0<w_1<w_2\), then \(\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w_2)\subseteq\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w_1)\); restricting a feasible profile to the cells active at \(w_2\) shows that \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\) is nonincreasing.  Also, the benchmark arm mean is a convex combination of \(\mu_0(x)\) and \(\mu_1(x)\), so the bounded-mean condition gives
\[
0\le\theta(P)\le2M.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)=\varnothing\) whenever \(w\ge M(1-2\delta)\), and consequently \(0\le w_{T,\rho}\le M(1-2\delta)<\infty\).

For any \(0<w<w_{T,\rho}\), monotonicity and the generalized-inverse definition give \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)>T\).  Every profile satisfying the context domination has total mass at most \(T\); hence for every uniformly budget-feasible design its induced profile must fail at least one information constraint.  There are therefore \(P\), an active \(\mathsf Q\), and \(P'\in\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)\) such that
\[
\mathrm{KL}(\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}\Vert\mathbb P_{P',\mathsf D}^{T})<\kappa_\delta,
\qquad
|\theta(P)-\theta(P')|>\frac{2w}{1-2\delta}.
\]
Taking the supremum over admissible pairs, the infimum over budget-feasible designs, and then the supremum over \(w<w_{T,\rho}\) gives
\[
\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\ge\frac{2w_{T,\rho}}{1-2\delta}.
\]
If the design class is empty, the same inequality holds by the stipulated extended value \(+\infty\).  Finally, the already-established coverage--information converse yields
\[
W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\ge\frac{1-2\delta}{2}\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\ge w_{T,\rho}.
\]
No step selects a baseline-independent occupation profile or constructs an interval, so the conclusion is only the necessary side of the relaxation.
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma proves that the corrected occupation program is a genuine procedure-free obstruction rather than an oracle allocation proposed by definition.
added_lemmas.gap: It supplies only the necessary direction; compatibility of its baseline-specific profiles with one law-independent sequential design is deliberately left open.
added_lemmas.consumer: The complete-frontier question inherits the explicit lower map \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\) while the attainment problem remains visible.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For the baseline-indexed occupation-measure programs \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\) and \(\mathcal D_{T,\rho}(w)\), determine whether there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(T\) and \(\rho\), for which the generalized inverse satisfies the boundary and no-overshoot relation
\[
\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w_{T,\rho})\le T
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w_{T,\rho})\ge cT
\]
whenever \(w_{T,\rho}>0\), or characterize exactly the discontinuities and inactive baseline--cell pairs that prevent such saturation.  Determine separately whether strong duality holds at the relevant levels; neither strong duality nor primal or dual attainment may be assumed.  Finally, prove or disprove that the baseline-indexed occupation profiles can be jointly realized, up to universal constants, by one predictable law-independent design and one connected \(1-\delta\) honest interval with participant-welfare loss at most \(\rho\), expected width of order \(w_{T,\rho}\), and stochastic context-arrival capacities respected.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original question was indexed by cell alone, omitted context-arrival and welfare constraints, and asked about the obsolete \(w_n\). The corrected question is narrowed to saturation, duality, and common sequential realization for the baseline-indexed occupation program.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Determine from the primitive H\"older--margin geometry an explicit piecewise function of \((T,\rho,\beta,\alpha,d,\delta)\) and prove that both \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) and \(\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) are equivalent to it up to constants throughout the feasible regime.  The derivation must evaluate the corrected baseline-indexed occupation relaxation, locate every budget branch and flattening threshold, and prove that one law-independent predictable design and one connected honest interval attain the upper side.  It must recover the proved \(\rho^{-1/2}\) fixed-gap edge, recover the fixed-design offline honest-width order when \(\rho\asymp T\), and settle the Gaussian early-kill case \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\).  No rate, saturation property, strong-duality identity, or realization claim is assumed.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frontier question must refer to the corrected budget-dependent occupation width and must not inherit the obsolete sign-switch cells, scalar quotas, or any assumed saturation or realization property.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For a baseline law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\), a cell \(\mathsf Q\in\mathscr Q\), and \(w>0\), define the complete coverage-separating local alternative set
\[
\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)
=\left\{P'\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}:
P'_X=P_X,\quad
\mu_a^{P'}(x)=\mu_a^P(x)\ \text{for every }x\in\mathcal X\setminus\mathsf Q\text{ and }a\in\mathcal A,\quad
|\theta(P')-\theta(P)|>\frac{2w}{1-2\delta}
\right\}.
\]
The active baseline--cell index set is
\[
\mathscr A(w)=\left\{(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\times\mathscr Q:
\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)\ne\varnothing\right\}.
\]
Thus every law with the same context marginal, the prescribed off-cell agreement, and coverage-calibrated target separation is included; no optimal-arm sign switch is required.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The prior alternatives were indexed only by a cell and excluded target-separating perturbations without an optimal-arm sign switch. The complete baseline-indexed set is the correct coverage obstruction.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \((P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)\), \(P'\in\mathcal S_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), and \(x\in\mathsf Q\), define the pointwise Gaussian information coefficient
\[
k_a(P,P';x)=\frac{\{\mu_a^P(x)-\mu_a^{P'}(x)\}^2}{2\sigma^2}.
\]
An arm-specific local occupation profile is a family \((\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) of finite nonnegative Borel measures supported on \(\mathsf Q\).  Its allocated information against \(P'\) is the exact integral
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int_{\mathsf Q}k_a(P,P';x)\,d\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x)
=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int_{\mathsf Q}
\frac{\{\mu_a^P(x)-\mu_a^{P'}(x)\}^2}{2\sigma^2}
\,d\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x).
\]
proposed_definition_changes.reason: A conditional-cell average multiplied by a scalar count is not the adaptive likelihood when assignments vary with context. Pointwise Gaussian information integrated against arm-specific occupation measures is exact.
The information constraints must range over all baseline-specific local alternatives and act on finite arm-specific occupation measures.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \(w>0\), define the worst-baseline occupation-measure primal value
\[
\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)
=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}}
\inf_{(\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a})}
\left\{
\sum_{\mathsf Q:(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(\mathsf Q)
\right\},
\]
where the inner infimum is over profiles satisfying all three conditions
\[
(\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a})_{a\in\mathcal A}\in\mathcal R_{P,\mathsf Q}(w)
\quad\text{for every }\mathsf Q\text{ with }(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w),
\]
\[
\sum_{\mathsf Q:(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(E)
\le T P_X(E)
\quad\text{for every Borel }E\subseteq\mathcal X,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{\mathsf Q:(P,\mathsf Q)\in\mathscr A(w)}
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
\int_{\mathsf Q}|\tau_P(x)|\mathbf 1\{a\ne\pi_P^\star(x)\}
\,d\nu_{P,\mathsf Q,a}(x)
\le\rho.
\]
The infimum of an empty feasible set is \(+\infty\).  The measure domination is the total-horizon and stochastic context-arrival constraint; in particular it implies that every feasible objective is at most \(T\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old separable sum omitted the horizon, random context-arrival capacities, the welfare budget, and the worst-baseline quantifier. The corrected primal includes each of them explicitly.
The corrected Lagrange lower value must price local alternatives, context capacity, and welfare simultaneously and impose its constraint pointwise for every active arm and context.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Define the budget- and horizon-dependent implicit occupation width by
\[
w_{T,\rho}=\inf\left\{w>0:\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\le T\right\},
\]
with the infimum taken in the extended nonnegative reals.  No power law, boundary closedness, or saturation identity is included in this definition.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Once allocation is constrained by both horizon and welfare, the inverse width necessarily depends on \(T\) and \(\rho\); the former \(w_n\) was budget-blind.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: The handle \(\mathsf H_{T,\rho}\) denotes the following unresolved realization program.  For levels \(w>w_{T,\rho}\) at which \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\le T\), use approximately feasible baseline-indexed occupation profiles and, when useful, feasible dual prices from \(\mathcal D_{T,\rho}(w)\); then seek one law-independent predictable assignment rule whose expected occupations simultaneously realize the relevant profiles subject to random context arrivals and welfare cost, together with one \(P\)-independent Borel map from the observed trajectory to a connected honest interval.  The handle names this program only: it is not itself an assignment kernel, an estimator, or an interval procedure, and it assumes neither primal--dual equality nor attainment.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The prior prose read as though quotas and an interval had already been constructed. The corrected handle names the unresolved coupling and inference program without claiming a design map or guarantee.

proposed.statement:
For the baseline-indexed occupation-measure programs \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\) and \(\mathcal D_{T,\rho}(w)\), determine whether there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(T\) and \(\rho\), for which the generalized inverse satisfies the boundary and no-overshoot relation
\[
\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w_{T,\rho})\le T
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w_{T,\rho})\ge cT
\]
whenever \(w_{T,\rho}>0\), or characterize exactly the discontinuities and inactive baseline--cell pairs that prevent such saturation.  Determine separately whether strong duality holds at the relevant levels; neither strong duality nor primal or dual attainment may be assumed.  Finally, prove or disprove that the baseline-indexed occupation profiles can be jointly realized, up to universal constants, by one predictable law-independent design and one connected \(1-\delta\) honest interval with participant-welfare loss at most \(\rho\), expected width of order \(w_{T,\rho}\), and stochastic context-arrival capacities respected.
proposed.justification: The corrected program isolates exact adaptive information, stochastic context capacity, and welfare cost before asking for a common sequential realization.
proposed.gap: Existing selective-exploration and adaptive-inference results do not prove saturation or common realization of baseline-indexed continuous-context occupation profiles under a hard welfare budget.
proposed.consumer: A positive result supplies the implementable upper half of the frontier; a negative result identifies an additional incompatibility or discontinuity branch.
proposed.partial_result:
The corrected programs admit two unconditional facts.  First, weak duality holds:
\[
\mathcal D_{T,\rho}(w)\le\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w).
\]
Second, every budget-feasible design and honest interval whose worst-law expected length is at most \(w\) induces baseline-indexed occupation measures feasible for \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\).  Hence
\[
\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\ge\frac{2w_{T,\rho}}{1-2\delta},
\qquad
W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\ge w_{T,\rho}.
\]
The remaining assertions are not consequences of weak duality: one still needs boundary closedness and no-overshoot control for \(w\mapsto\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\), any desired strong-duality theorem, and a coupling of the baseline-specific profiles into one predictable law-independent design and one connected honest interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the open question's claim, dependencies, symbols, and partial result with the corrected occupation-measure construction.

proposed.statement: Determine from the primitive H\"older--margin geometry an explicit piecewise function of \((T,\rho,\beta,\alpha,d,\delta)\) and prove that both \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) and \(\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) are equivalent to it up to constants throughout the feasible regime.  The derivation must evaluate the corrected baseline-indexed occupation relaxation, locate every budget branch and flattening threshold, and prove that one law-independent predictable design and one connected honest interval attain the upper side.  It must recover the proved \(\rho^{-1/2}\) fixed-gap edge, recover the fixed-design offline honest-width order when \(\rho\asymp T\), and settle the Gaussian early-kill case \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\).  No rate, saturation property, strong-duality identity, or realization claim is assumed.
proposed.justification: This remains the theorem-level kernel: an explicit rate and all transitions must be derived from the corrected occupation geometry and attained by one actual experiment.
proposed.gap: No cited result combines all-design honest-length converses, nonregular optimal-value geometry, stochastic context capacity, and a hard participant-welfare budget.
proposed.consumer: The completed map would give trialists the shortest credible post-trial statement about personalization gain compatible with a chosen welfare budget.
proposed.partial_result:
Below the feasibility boundary, \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})=+\infty\).  In every feasible regime the constant interval \([0,2M]\) is honest, while the corrected occupation relaxation and the coverage converse give
\[
w_{T,\rho}
\le W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\le2M,
\qquad
\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})
\ge\frac{2w_{T,\rho}}{1-2\delta}.
\]
Under the stated interior fixed-gap compatibility and for \(C_1\log T\le\rho\le c_1T\), monotonicity from the fixed-gap subclass to the full class and the proved fixed-gap theorem additionally give the compulsory lower branch
\[
W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\ge c\rho^{-1/2}.
\]
Thus the certified lower envelope is the maximum of the implicit occupation obstruction and the fixed-gap obstruction, whereas only the constant upper bound is currently available over the full class.  In the early-kill specialization \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\), feasibility is exactly at order \(T^{3/5}\) and the compulsory fixed-gap lower term is \(T^{-3/10}\).  Evaluating \(w_{T,\rho}\), locating the H\"older-local branches, and attaining them by one design and interval remain open.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the frontier question with the corrected implicit width and remove any dependence on the obsolete scalar allocation program.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove or refute boundary saturation for \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}\), determine any strong-duality conditions beyond the proved weak inequality, and couple the baseline-indexed occupation profiles into one predictable law-independent design and one connected honest interval.
open_obligations.obstruction: The corrected primal deliberately optimizes a different occupation profile for every baseline law. Feasibility for each baseline does not imply compatibility with a single history-dependent kernel. Moreover, monotonicity of \(w\mapsto\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\) does not give right closedness or a uniform lower multiple at its generalized inverse, and the handle contains no interval endpoints or coverage calculation.
open_obligations.attempted: Replaced scalar quotas by exact occupation measures, embedded every actual adaptive design into the capacity and welfare constraints, proved the trajectory-KL identity for every local alternative through the existing Gaussian decomposition, and derived weak Lagrange duality. These steps certify necessity but do not supply the missing common-design coupling.
open_obligations.partial_result: Weak duality and the necessity of the corrected occupation relaxation are proved, including \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\) and \(\Omega_{T,\delta}\ge2w_{T,\rho}/(1-2\delta)\).  What remains is boundary saturation, any stronger duality statement, and joint sequential realization.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Evaluate \(w_{T,\rho}\) from H\"older--margin geometry, derive every local branch and flattening threshold, and construct one budget-feasible adaptive design with a connected honest interval attaining the resulting full-class width.
open_obligations.obstruction: The corrected program gives a necessary baselinewise relaxation, but its law-specific feasible profiles are not yet jointly realizable. The frozen bump lemma does not by itself evaluate the occupation program or construct the nonsmooth positive-part interval, so an explicit upper rate would still assume the central exploration-and-inference step.
open_obligations.attempted: Combined the established feasibility boundary, coverage converse, fixed-gap frontier, and bump family with the corrected occupation formulation. The new design-embedding lemma yields an implicit procedure-free lower bound, but no honest derivation converts it into a closed H\"older exponent or matching estimator.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved bracket is \(\max\{w_{T,\rho},c\rho^{-1/2}\}\le W_{T,\delta}\le2M\) under the stated fixed-gap interior compatibility and \(C_1\log T\le\rho\le c_1T\), while \(w_{T,\rho}\le W_{T,\delta}\le2M\) throughout the feasible regime.  Below feasibility \(W_{T,\delta}=+\infty\), and the early-kill fixed-gap term is \(T^{-3/10}\).  The value of \(w_{T,\rho}\) and an attaining full-class construction remain open.

prose_updates.tldr: An adaptive experiment that protects current participants suppresses observations from inferior treatments, while honest inference on the gain from individualized targeting needs those observations and is nonregular near treatment ties. The proved results establish class nonemptiness, the feasibility boundary, an all-procedure coverage-to-information converse, and the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) frontier. The corrected general construction is a baseline-indexed occupation-measure relaxation: it includes every same-context-law, off-cell-agreeing target-separating alternative, uses exact pointwise Gaussian information, and enforces stochastic context capacity and participant welfare. Every narrow honest procedure must satisfy this relaxation, and its Lagrange price program obeys weak duality. Saturation, strong duality, an explicit H\"older-local rate, and realization of the baseline-specific profiles by one law-independent adaptive design and connected interval remain open; the \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) case remains the mandatory early kill test.

project_justification.gap: Existing regret--inference Pareto results treat point-estimation error in finite-arm, finite-feature, or finitely stratified models, while adaptive confidence-interval results generally take logging propensities as given and optimal-value inference does not price exploration by participant welfare. None combines a common observed-trajectory interval, nonregular positive-part geometry, continuous-context arrival capacity, and a hard uniform welfare budget. The remaining gap is not a missing scalar allocation formula: it is saturation and common sequential realization of baseline-indexed occupation profiles.
project_justification.niche: The targeting gain \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\) combines a regular benchmark term with a nonsmooth positive-part term. A welfare budget makes information endogenous because an arm's local information is integrated against a context-dependent occupation measure while its cost is the baseline gap. This produces a baseline-indexed sequential modulus with stochastic context-capacity constraints.
project_justification.fill: The procedure-free coverage theorem converts target separation and adaptive Gaussian information into a lower bound for every design and interval. The corrected local sets include all same-context-law alternatives agreeing off a cell whose target separation exceeds \(2w/(1-2\delta)\), without a sign-switch restriction. Arm-specific occupation measures yield the exact information integral; the global primal enforces context-arrival domination and welfare cost before taking the worst baseline. A Lagrange price program has proved weak duality, and every honest width-\(w\) procedure induces a primal-feasible profile, giving \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\). The open kernel is to evaluate and saturate this implicit width and to realize its baseline-specific profiles by one predictable design and connected honest interval.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No attaining nuisance estimator is currently part of the core. The corrected object is an occupation-measure relaxation. Any upper theorem must explicitly construct predictable regression or approximation estimates, interval endpoints, bias control, and coverage from the realized adaptive sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Perchet and Rigollet supply the cited H\"older--margin regret exponent used only for the feasibility boundary. Simchi-Levi and Wang establish a finite-arm regret--estimation frontier, and Li, Shi, and Simchi-Levi balance regret and CATE error over finitely many contexts; neither resolves continuous-context honest width under a hard welfare budget. Hu, Kallus, and Mao motivate selective local exploration, while Hadad and coauthors, Bibaut and coauthors, Waudby-Smith and coauthors, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, and Shen and coauthors provide adaptive-score or stability tools when the logging design or regular target is supplied. Luedtke and van der Laan and Ponomarev and Semenova address nonregular optimal-welfare inference without optimizing welfare-constrained data collection. Kaufmann, Capp\'e, and Garivier support the adaptive Gaussian change-of-measure step, and Cai and Low support the coverage-to-length logic. None of these sources proves saturation, strong duality, or law-independent sequential realization for the corrected baseline-indexed occupation relaxation; those claims remain open rather than being imported from prior work.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The occupation program is a necessary baselinewise relaxation, not an estimator. Its inner optimizer may depend on the unknown baseline law, and separate feasible profiles need not be compatible with one predictable law-independent design. Monotonicity alone does not control a jump at \(w_{T,\rho}\), and weak duality alone does not yield strong duality or attainment. The bump lemma and regret packing do not by themselves evaluate the scalar targeting-gain width because target contributions can cancel and adaptive allocation can concentrate on selected contexts.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established scope consists of class nonemptiness, the cited feasibility exponent with its Gaussian transfer, the all-design coverage--information converse, the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) theorem, the target-separating bump construction, weak duality for the corrected occupation programs, and the necessary bounds \(\Omega_{T,\delta}\ge2w_{T,\rho}/(1-2\delta)\) and \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\). The width and modulus equal \(+\infty\) when the uniformly feasible design class is empty. The exact H\"older-local rate, saturation and boundary regularity of \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}\), strong duality or attainment, and realization by one predictable design and connected interval remain answer-open. At \(\rho\asymp T\), a completed result must recover fixed-design honest inference; on the fixed-gap subclass it must recover \(\rho^{-1/2}\); below \(T^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\), the design class is empty.
